coverage_planes.current_mechanism: Deleting auth.users cascades through subject and owner workspace foreign keys, but the delete-account runtime neither names nor independently verifies these rows.
coverage_planes.required_proof: Explicit workspace discovery, row-count receipt for all eleven tables, transactional or resumable execution and post-delete verification.

coverage_planes.current_mechanism: R13 proves local derivative erasure only; none of R10 through R13 is migrated or runtime-connected.
coverage_planes.required_proof: Migration review, Supabase parity, concurrency and runtime caller.

coverage_planes.current_mechanism: A manually maintained delete list plus a two-pass sweep handles some user_id tables.
coverage_planes.required_proof: Schema-derived ownership registry, FK-order plan and zero-row verification for every owned table.

coverage_planes.current_mechanism: Briefing rows and up to 1000 root-prefix objects in ctrl-briefings are attempted. External email copies and provider retention are not controlled.
coverage_planes.required_proof: Recursive paginated storage deletion, signed-URL expiry accounting, cache ownership, provider retention and honest external-copy disclosure.

coverage_planes.current_mechanism: Database rows are in the manual sweep, but delete-account does not purge the skill-packages bucket. User-controlled and third-party copies have no recall mechanism.
coverage_planes.required_proof: Purge owned storage objects, record export destinations and distinguish local deletion from copies the user or another provider controls.

coverage_planes.current_mechanism: mcp_pulls is swept; token revocation is not an explicit first step and downstream copied context is not retractable.
coverage_planes.required_proof: Revoke credentials before data deletion, verify no usable token remains and disclose downstream-copy limits.

coverage_planes.current_mechanism: Ownership is inconsistent. Some caches have no user key. Audit rows intentionally survive, and the current deletion runtime writes the user's email into retained audit metadata.
coverage_planes.required_proof: Purpose-specific retention, identifier redaction or keyed pseudonymisation, attributable cache eviction and a legal retention schedule.

coverage_planes.current_mechanism: The repository sends data to processors but has no unified processing receipt or deletion orchestration. Stripe subscription cancellation is attempted, not customer-record deletion.
coverage_planes.required_proof: Per-provider data classification, retention terms, request identifiers, deletion capability and evidence receipt.
Retention windows, restore-time suppression, log redaction and a plain-language boundary for user-controlled copies.

blocking_findings: delete-account returns success true even when deletionErrors is non-empty; the UI contract catches this only in a skipped E2E test
the deletion E2E suite is skipped and verifies only a small table subset
skill-packages storage is written by generate-skill-export but is absent from account deletion
storage deletion lists one page of at most 1000 root-prefix objects and is not recursively proven
retained audit events include the user's email in metadata after an erasure request
canonical Brain deletion currently relies on eventual auth-user cascade without explicit coverage evidence
external AI, email, audio, billing and spreadsheet processors have no unified deletion receipt
next_gate: Design a provider-aware, schema-derived erasure plan and receipt. Do not edit the live delete-account path until exact retention exceptions, external-copy language and failure semantics are approved.
bounded_claim: R14 is a repository-evidenced deletion coverage map. It proves neither complete account erasure nor any provider deletion. Its purpose is to prevent R13's prepared-derivative proof from being misrepresented as whole-Brain deletion.
